system: You are the lead AI reviewer (orchestrator) on a deal team. Your cheap parser subagents have read the data room and returned the compact findings below. Compile a concise DD summary for the partner: key findings, red flags, and a clear recommendation on whether to proceed.

exchanges.user:
===== PARSER FINDINGS =====
| Document | What it is and what the deal partner should know |
|---|---|
| **L01 – NDA** | Mutual NDA with Halden Partners; two-year term, standard carve-outs, and no non-solicitation restriction. |
| **L02 – Lease** | Head office lease at Level 3, 41 Coolidge Street, for five years from 2024; market rent review in year three. Assignment needs landlord consent, but a change of control is expressly not an assignment. |
| **L03 – Management accounts** | FY revenue of AUD 18.4m, up 9%, with 61% gross margin. Material customer concentration: Arlen Health accounts for 41% of revenue; the next-largest customer is 7%. |
| **L04 – HR** | 94 employees on standard contracts. CTO and Head of Sales have signed 12-month retention letters. |
| **L05 – Customer contract** | Five-year Arlen Health MSA renewed 1 July 2025 for platform licence, hosting and support. Annual CPI-indexed fees are invoiced quarterly in advance. 99.9% monthly uptime SLA; service credits capped at 10% of monthly fees. Liability is capped at 12 months’ fees, except data breaches at 3× annual fees. Key deal issue: Arlen may terminate for convenience, without an early-termination fee, on 90 days’ notice during the six months after a supplier change of control. Confirm timing and transaction-trigger implications; together with the 41% revenue concentration, this is a material retention risk. |
| **L06 – Bank facility** | AUD 6m revolving facility expires 2027; quarterly net-debt-to-EBITDA covenant capped at 2.5×. |
| **L07 – CFO email** | Reports a 31 March covenant breach: 2.9× versus 2.5× limit. Bank had not been notified as of the 14 April email; CFO planned to raise it after the board meeting. Material financing and disclosure issue—confirm notice, waiver, default consequences, and current covenant status promptly. |
| **L08 – Internal note** | Customer Success lead raises a tentative possibility that the January price change contributed to small-business churn. Evidence is expressly uncertain and numbers are small; treat as an unverified retention signal and request supporting cohort/churn data. |
| **L09 – Insurance** | Professional indemnity and cyber cover of AUD 10m, renewed in March; no notified claims. Confirm policy limits, exclusions, and continuity if relevant. |
| **L10 – IP** | Platform code is employee-authored under standard IP assignment clauses. Two open-source components use MIT and Apache 2.0 licences; verify compliance and any third-party code inventory. |
| **L11 – Supplier** | Hosting from a major cloud provider on standard online terms, monthly billed with no minimum commitment. Review terms for termination, service levels, data handling, and any change-of-control provisions. |
| **L12 – Board minutes** | 20 March board minutes approve FY budget and hiring plan and note a strong sales pipeline; no other business recorded. |
| **L13 – Policy** | Privacy policy updated for the 2025 amendments; annual staff privacy training completed. |
| **L14 – Vendor contract** | Office cleaning contract runs for 12 months and is terminable on 30 days’ notice. |
| **L15 – Fixed assets** | Laptops and office fit-out with written-down value of AUD 0.4m.

Write the DD summary now.
exchanges.text:
## DD summary — recommendation: proceed conditionally

**Do not commit unconditionally.** Two material issues require resolution: retention of Arlen Health following a change of control and the reported bank covenant breach.

### Key findings and red flags
- **Customer concentration / transaction-triggered exit:** Arlen contributes **41% of revenue** (approximately AUD 7.5m). Despite its five-year MSA, it may terminate without an early-termination fee on 90 days’ notice during the six months after a supplier change of control. Confirm the trigger and notice mechanics; seek a binding waiver or retention commitment and assess downside valuation if unavailable. **[L03, L05]**
- **Financing / unresolved breach:** The CFO reported 31 March leverage of **2.9× against a 2.5× covenant**. The bank had not been notified as of 14 April; subsequent notification, waiver and current compliance are unknown. Confirm default consequences, facility availability and any transaction consents. **[L06–L07]**
- **Trading:** FY revenue was **AUD 18.4m, up 9%, with 61% gross margin**. Small-business churn potentially linked to January pricing is explicitly unverified; obtain cohort data before drawing conclusions. EBITDA, cash conversion and current trading still need validation. **[L03, L08]**

### Other findings
- CTO and Head of Sales have signed 12-month retention letters; confirm their commencement dates and terms. **[L04]**
- Lease expressly excludes change of control from assignment, although year-three market rent review creates cost uncertainty. **[L02]**
- Employee IP assignments and identified MIT/Apache components are encouraging, subject to ownership and licence-compliance verification. **[L10]**
- AUD 10m PI/cyber cover and privacy training are reported, but coverage and operational compliance remain untested. Arlen’s data-breach liability cap is 3× annual fees; assess potential exposure against actual insurance coverage. **[L05, L09, L13]**
- Review hosting continuity, termination rights and data-handling terms. **[L11]**

### Conditions to proceed
Require satisfactory **Arlen retention protection** and **documented lender resolution or replacement financing** before an unconditional commitment. Validate earnings, cash flow and churn, then reflect residual risks in price and transaction protections. If either principal issue remains unresolved, **pause the deal**.

*Based on parser findings only; underlying documents have not been independently verified.*
